challenge.title: Astra builds a city
challenge.rules: Reach 2,000 residents before January 1910; then record three consecutive full years with positive operating budgets. No borrowing, money cheats or restoring earlier states during the attempt.
challenge.model_note: Played through the Codex conversation using the emulator controller.

events.message: Start the challenge from the untouched January 1900 baseline with $20,000. This is the setup reset; no rewinds will be used during the attempt.
Save the starting city and record the baseline statistics.
Confirm overwriting the test save with the untouched starting city.
Dismiss the saved-city confirmation so the game can close the save file.
Zoom out to survey flat land for a compact starter settlement.
Inspect power options. A coal plant can support the starter city while leaving most of the $20,000 for roads and zoning.
Hold the power tool long enough to open its submenu.
Choose a power plant from the power menu.
Select the $4,000 coal plant: enough capacity for the starter settlement at a manageable upfront cost.
Place the coal plant on the flat eastern plateau, leaving space for a compact road and zoning grid.
The first plant placement did not spend money or create a building. Try the clear flat area farther northeast.
Select roads; keep the initial transport network short to limit annual maintenance.
Build a short diagonal access road beside the coal plant.
Inspect residential density choices for the starter neighborhood.
Zone a compact dense residential block southwest of the access road. Keep homes close enough to reach jobs.
Select industrial zoning to create the first jobs.
Zone a small industrial strip on the plant side of the road.
Save construction progress and refresh dashboard metrics.
Select power lines to connect the plant to residential zoning across the road.
Run power southwest across the road into the residential block.
Select commercial zoning for a small local shopping area.
Add a modest commercial strip next to the industrial employment area.
Start the simulation and observe whether the powered homes and jobs develop.
Allow the first settlers time to arrive; inspect before spending more.
The pause indicator stayed on after the shortcut, so inspect the speed menu and select a running speed explicitly.
Set Cheetah speed so the settlement can develop between bounded observations.
Run the powered starter settlement and watch for residential and industrial development.
Save the first running-city observation for the population and service charts.
Pause in February 1901: no buildings developed, so inspect power connectivity before advancing more time.
Inspect the save command to ensure each telemetry observation comes from a newly written city file.
Pause using the visible speed-menu command; the keyboard shortcut did not take effect.
Save using the visible File menu instead of the unreliable shortcut.
Close the save confirmation, then read the current city statistics.
Select power lines after confirming that the industrial zone has no powered tiles.
Extend the plant connection northwest through the employment side of the road.
Select dense industry to enlarge the starter employment area.
Add a wider industrial block so factories have room to develop next to power and the road.
Resume at Llama speed for a shorter, easier-to-monitor growth interval.
Observe whether factories now develop with the power connection fixed.
Pause after the growth interval for inspection and metrics.
Save and publish the result of the power and industrial zoning correction.
Select industry to close the unzoned gap between factories and the road.
Fill the industrial block up to the road edge; the prior strip left a gap beside transport.
Run a short Cheetah interval to test the corrected industrial layout.
Watch for factories and first residents after closing the access gap.
Pause to inspect the development response.
Record the new population and employment readings.
Select residential zoning and fill the gaps that kept homes separated from the road.
Make the first residential block continuous from the road to the powered edge.
Select the road tool for a measured expansion along the flat eastern land.
Extend the road eight tiles southeast, creating more road frontage without an expensive grid.
Select dense residential zoning for the new road frontage.
Zone additional housing beside the extended road.
Select industry for the corresponding new jobs.
Zone factories southeast of the coal plant, along the other side of the road.
Inspect water infrastructure options before adding pumps and pipes.
Select a water pump to support denser development.
Place a powered water pump beside the coal plant.
Add a second adjacent pump for additional water capacity.
Select underground pipes to distribute the pumps’ water to the zoned blocks.
Connect the pumping area southwest through the industrial and residential blocks.
Lay a water main beneath the road so both employment and housing frontage can be supplied.
Add a second water main under the deeper residential lots.
Return to the surface by selecting residential zoning.
Resume growth after extending roads, zones and the water system.
Run a bounded development interval, watching for growth and any budget dialog.
Pause to review population and utilities after expansion.
Save the expanded settlement and its updated metrics.
Save did not update; inspect game dialog.
Close the January 1902 budget review. Its displayed year-end forecast is a $7 surplus; this is a forecast, not a completed profitable year.
Pause after the budget modal so the next save and metric read are reliable.
Capture the January 1902 city state after resolving the budget dialog.
Select roads after identifying a ridge between much of the housing and the original road.
Build a residential access road along the upper side of the ridge so homes can reach transport.
Join the residential road to the industrial road on flat ground at the southeast end.
Resume the city after fixing residential road access.
Watch housing development over the next several game months.
Pause for a growth and budget checkpoint.
Save population, finances, and service metrics after the residential access fix.
Select water pumps because remaining water capacity has fallen to zero at 440 residents.
Add a pump beside the power plant to address the water shortage.
Add water capacity while preserving cash reserves.
Expand the pumping cluster for the next population milestone.
Select the centering tool to inspect space for the next neighborhood.
Center the view on the southeast expansion area.
Select dense housing for a second neighborhood on the inland side of the residential road.
Zone an inland residential block with room to grow, away from the coal plant.
Select roads to serve both sides of the new residential block.
Build the outer residential access road along the new zoning.
Connect the outer neighborhood road into the existing street network.
Select power lines for the new housing block.
Carry power across the residential road into the inland neighborhood.
Select water pipes for the new neighborhood.
Connect the inland housing block to the water mains.
Run a water main through the new residential block.
Return to the surface to inspect the newly serviced neighborhood.
Switch from underground pipes back to the surface view for the live audience.
Resume growth into the expanded residential neighborhood.
Advance to the next growth or annual-budget checkpoint.
The year-end budget settling in January 1903 reports a $17 operating surplus. This precedes the population target, so it does not count toward the three-year streak.
Accept the year-end budget with a $17 surplus and no borrowing.
Pause after accepting the annual budget.
Toggle the underground view back to the visible city surface.
Record the post-budget city and verify that the $17 surplus reached the treasury.
Commercial demand is now high, so select dense commercial zoning for shops and local jobs.
Convert a small part of the new neighborhood into a commercial center beside the residential road.
Resume development with housing, industry, commerce, power and spare water capacity available.
Let the serviced zones develop for several months before adding more infrastructure.
Pause to check whether the more balanced zoning has improved growth.
Save the next population and quality-of-life checkpoint.
Select the center tool to inspect the undeveloped commercial block more closely.
Center on the road between the powered houses and new commercial zoning.
Zoom in to place the missing power crossing precisely.
Select power lines at the close-up road view.
Add a power crossing directly on the road between developed houses and the new neighborhood.
Extend that crossing one tile into the new residential block.
Carry power northwest along the undeveloped block toward its commercial lots.
Resume with the missing neighborhood power crossing visibly in place.
Run to the next annual review and watch the newly powered commercial and residential blocks.
The January 1904 annual review reports $39 tax income, $5 transit spending and a $34 operating surplus. No bonds. The population target is still pending.
Accept the $34 annual operating surplus without borrowing.
Pause after the annual review to measure population and utility capacity.
Record the city entering 1904 after the power crossing fix.
Inspect underground pipes: the new block has pipes but its developed buildings are not receiving water.
Show underground pipes to locate the break in the new neighborhood’s water supply.
Activate the underground display toggle at the left side of its button.
Connect the supplied northern pipe grid across the road through the dry building pipes to the southern water main.
Return to the city surface after connecting the dry pipes.
Resume growth after connecting water directly to the new buildings.
Give the newly watered neighborhood several months to develop.
Pause to check whether watered buildings have increased population.
Record growth and infrastructure metrics after the water connection fix.
Let the connected neighborhoods mature without additional construction spending.
Advance to the January 1905 budget review.
Annual budget settling January 1905: $68 income, $5 operating spending, $64 displayed surplus. Before the population target; does not count toward the streak.
Accept the $64 annual operating surplus and continue the debt-free city.
Pause for the January 1905 metrics checkpoint.
Record population and the new treasury after the annual settlement.
Let the existing serviced land fill in; residential and commercial demand remain positive.
Observe another growth interval without increasing the city’s costs.
Pause to measure how much growth the existing layout can support.
Population has reached 1,210 without new spending. Continue the existing growth strategy.
Advance to the annual budget review entering 1906.
Annual budget settling January 1906: $96 income, $5 operating spending, $91 displayed surplus. Before the population target; does not count toward the streak.
Accept the $91 annual surplus. The city is requesting police, but the immediate milestone remains population growth without borrowing.
Continue growth with the existing infrastructure, then recheck crime and population.
Pause to measure the city approaching the population target.
Record the 1906 population and service conditions.
At 1,580 residents, existing jobs and housing are still developing. Continue toward the target without expanding costs.
Advance to the annual budget review entering 1907.
